documents: Passport, proof of foreign address (utility bill), bank reference letter, source-of-funds declaration, TIN if available.
min_deposit_fees: Guides cite from about XCD 300 at local banks up to around USD 5,000 at international-oriented banks; fees not published.
banks: Global Bank of Commerce, ACB Caribbean, Republic Bank (Antigua) cited by guides; Canadian banks reported exiting.
restrictions: Strict KYC/AML and CRS reporting to home tax authority; correspondent de-risking means scrutiny of non-resident clients; US persons face FATCA.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut held abroad; offshore/international banks licensed by the FSRC.
cost_note: Cheapest cited option is a local bank opening deposit of about XCD 300 (USD 1 = XCD 2.70, fixed peg), while opening and monthly fees are not published (web search budget exhausted in pass 2, so figures come from the existing min_deposit_fees text and were not re-verified against a bank tariff).

documents: Passport with entry stamp, local proof of address (hotel/lease letter), NIT tax ID from SAT, home bank reference letter, initial deposit.
min_deposit_fees: Reports range from about GTQ 500 to USD 1,000+ for USD accounts; not officially published.
banks: Banco Industrial and BAM reported as most flexible for foreigners.
restrictions: Physical presence usually required; branch-level discretion is high; USD accounts subject to extra KYC and source-of-funds checks.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut cards for local ATM use; remittance services.
cost_note: Banco Industrial/BAM opening deposit reported from about GTQ 500 (USD 1 = GTQ 7.7), with USD accounts needing USD 1,000+, and opening and monthly fees not published (web search budget exhausted in pass 2, so figures come from the existing min_deposit_fees text and were not re-verified against a bank tariff).

documents: Passport, usually a valid visa or cedula, proof of address, employment certificate or RUC, personal reference from an Ecuadorian citizen.
banks: Banco Pichincha (passport plus visa reported), BanEcuador (accepts passport), some savings cooperatives.
restrictions: Most banks require a cedula (residency); economy is dollarised so accounts are in USD; strict AML checks on foreign funds.
alternatives: Savings and credit cooperatives; Wise/Revolut for USD; foreign cards at ATMs.
cost_note: Banco Pichincha, BanEcuador and cooperatives publish no non-resident opening fee, minimum deposit or monthly fee (web search budget exhausted in pass 2, so figures come from the existing min_deposit_fees text and were not re-verified against a bank tariff).

documents: Chilean ID card (cedula de extranjeria) with RUT, visa/residence, proof of local address and often local income.
min_deposit_fees: CuentaRUT has no minimum; checking accounts typically need income around CLP 800,000/month; non-resident fees not published.
banks: none known for non-residents; BancoEstado CuentaRUT and Scotiabank foreigner accounts need residence/visa.
restrictions: RUT and Chilean ID required; banks generally cannot open accounts from abroad for non-residents.
alternatives: Brokerage accounts (high minimums), Wise/Revolut, foreign cards.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts here (CuentaRUT and foreigner accounts need a RUT and residence/visa), so no costs apply.

documents: Passport with valid long-term pass (employment, student, MM2H), proof of address, reference letter; tourist visas generally not accepted.
min_deposit_fees: Typically about MYR 250-1,000 for savings/current accounts; non-resident fees not published.
banks: Maybank and CIMB cited as foreigner-friendly; HSBC/Standard Chartered premier tiers case-by-case.
restrictions: Non-residents fall under BNM foreign exchange policy as External Accounts; first account must be opened in branch.
alternatives: Wise (may require pass), e-wallets for visitors, international private banking in Labuan.
cost_note: Maybank/CIMB savings accounts reported at about MYR 250 minimum (up to MYR 1,000 for current accounts; USD 1 = MYR 4.2), with non-resident opening and monthly fees not published (web search budget exhausted in pass 2, so figures come from the existing min_deposit_fees text and were not re-verified against a bank tariff).

documents: Passport, proof of address, visa or residence documentation, and source of funds; banks follow BCTL KYC instructions.
banks: BNU (CGD group), ANZ Timor-Leste, BNCTL, Bank Mandiri branch.
restrictions: Small USD-based banking sector; strict identification under BCTL instructions; non-resident acceptance is case-by-case.
alternatives: Keep Australian bank account; Wise/Revolut; ANZ group relationship from Australia.
cost_note: BNU, ANZ, BNCTL and Mandiri publish no non-resident opening fee, minimum deposit or monthly fee (USD is the local currency) (web search budget exhausted in pass 2, so figures come from the existing min_deposit_fees text and were not re-verified against a bank tariff).

documents: Passport and identification per ANZ terms, residential address, likely purpose of account and local connection.
min_deposit_fees: ANZ foreign currency account fee USD 5/month; other fees per ANZ Kiribati schedule; minimum deposit not published.
banks: ANZ Bank (Kiribati) Limited, Development Bank of Kiribati.
restrictions: Foreign currency accounts subject to the Exchange Control Ordinance; very small market with limited non-resident service.
alternatives: Keep Australian bank (AUD is legal tender); Wise; remittance services.
cost_note: ANZ Kiribati foreign currency account fee of USD 5/month, with opening fee and minimum deposit not published (AUD is the local currency) (web search budget exhausted in pass 2, so figures come from the existing min_deposit_fees text and were not re-verified against a bank tariff).

documents: Passport, IIN (obtained in person at a public service centre), Kazakh phone number, document showing legal basis of stay (entry stamp/visa), home TIN for CRS.
min_deposit_fees: Basic card accounts generally free to open; premium tiers higher; specific non-resident fees not published.
banks: Kaspi Bank, Halyk Bank, Bank CenterCredit, ForteBank, Freedom Bank.
restrictions: Remote opening closed since 2025; non-resident cards valid max 12 months; sanctions-related scrutiny for Russian flows; CRS reporting.
alternatives: Freedom Finance brokerage, Wise, Revolut.
cost_note: Kaspi Gold basic card account is free to open with no minimum balance and no monthly service fee (KZT, about 520 per USD); premium tiers cost more and non-resident-specific fees are not published (web search budget exhausted in pass 2, so figures come from the existing min_deposit_fees text and were not re-verified against a bank tariff).

documents: Passport (6+ months validity), visa or residence permit, proof of Congolese address (lease, utility bill or accommodation certificate), TIN if available, initial deposit.
banks: Societe Generale Congo, BGFIBank Congo, BCI (Banque Commerciale Internationale) cited by guides; non-residents rated difficult.
restrictions: CEMAC/BEAC foreign exchange regulation restricts transfers out of the zone; heavy KYC for non-residents; XAF accounts.
alternatives: Mobile money (MTN MoMo, Airtel Money) needs local SIM/ID; Wise/foreign bank accounts.
cost_note: Societe Generale, BGFIBank and BCI Congo publish no non-resident opening fee, minimum deposit or monthly fee (web search budget exhausted in pass 2, so figures come from the existing min_deposit_fees text and were not re-verified against a bank tariff).

documents: Passport, KRA PIN (or KRA private ruling exemption), local referee/introducer, proof of address, passport photos.
banks: Diamond Trust Bank and Standard Chartered reported anecdotally; Equity and KCB diaspora accounts target Kenyans.
restrictions: KRA PIN required for any account; each bank sets its own non-resident policy; diaspora products mostly for Kenyan nationals.
alternatives: M-Pesa (needs Kenyan SIM registered with passport), Wise, Revolut.
cost_note: DTB and Standard Chartered Kenya publish no non-resident terms, and diaspora accounts target Kenyans (web search budget exhausted in pass 2, so figures come from the existing min_deposit_fees text and were not re-verified against a bank tariff).

documents: Certified passport/ID copy, proof of foreign residence (lease, utility bill, bank statement or affidavit), passport photo, application form.
min_deposit_fees: Steward Bank non-resident FCA: USD 20 opening deposit and USD 5 service fee; others not published.
banks: Steward Bank (non-resident FCA via diaspora banking); other banks case-by-case.
restrictions: RBZ exchange controls; non-resident FCAs in USD; currency export limits and customs declarations; history of currency instability.
alternatives: EcoCash mobile money (local SIM), Wise/remittance services to Zimbabwe.
cost_note: Steward Bank non-resident FCA with a USD 20 opening deposit and a USD 5 service fee, assumed monthly, while the opening fee is not published (web search budget exhausted in pass 2, so figures come from the existing min_deposit_fees text and were not re-verified against a bank tariff).

documents: Passport, proof of address (Meldezettel usually requested; foreign address may be accepted case-by-case), TIN/CRS self-certification, proof of income/source of funds.
min_deposit_fees: Typical current accounts cost roughly EUR 3-10/month; non-resident terms not published.
banks: Erste Bank (branch only for non-residents per guides); others case-by-case.
restrictions: Online onboarding (e.g. George) restricted to Austrian residents; EU basic account right covers EU legal residents only; strict AML and CRS reporting.
alternatives: N26, Revolut, Wise (EUR IBAN; eligibility depends on residence).
cost_note: Erste Bank-type current accounts cost roughly EUR 3-10/month, low end shown (EUR 1 = USD 1.17), with non-resident opening fee and minimum deposit not published (web search budget exhausted in pass 2, so figures come from the existing min_deposit_fees text and were not re-verified against a bank tariff).

documents: Passport; usually residence permit and address card (lakcimkartya) or proof of rental; some banks accept passport only.
min_deposit_fees: OTP foreign currency accounts reported with no minimum deposit; other fees not published.
banks: OTP Bank and others case-by-case; some banks refuse non-residents by policy.
restrictions: Physical presence usually required; non-resident accounts may be limited to foreign-currency accounts; CRS reporting.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut (EU IBAN).
cost_note: OTP Bank foreign currency account reported with no minimum deposit, with opening and monthly fees not published (HUF about 335 per USD) (web search budget exhausted in pass 2, so figures come from the existing min_deposit_fees text and were not re-verified against a bank tariff).

documents: Passport (often with notarised Ukrainian translation), tax registration number (RNOKPP), and in practice usually a residence permit.
banks: none known reliably; PrivatBank and others reported to require residence permits in practice.
restrictions: Martial law since 2022 with NBU currency controls and cross-border transfer limits; non-resident current accounts legally allowed since 2019 but banks often refuse.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut, foreign bank accounts.
cost_note: No bank reliably opens accounts for non-residents without a residence permit, and no non-resident fees are published (web search budget exhausted in pass 2, so figures come from the existing min_deposit_fees text and were not re-verified against a bank tariff).

documents: Passport and Icelandic kennitala (or non-resident system ID from Registers Iceland), electronic ID for app onboarding.
banks: none known for pure non-residents; Arion, Landsbankinn, Islandsbanki require kennitala.
restrictions: Kennitala required by all banks; non-resident system IDs usually tied to employment or property; no remote onboarding for non-residents.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut; foreign cards widely accepted.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts here (Arion, Landsbankinn and Islandsbanki require a kennitala), so no costs apply.

documents: Passport, foreign proof of address, Portuguese NIF (obtainable via fiscal representative), proof of income/source of funds, CRS tax self-certification.
min_deposit_fees: Opening deposit around EUR 250 at some banks; intermediary remote packages roughly EUR 270-700; monthly fees vary.
banks: Millennium bcp, Caixa Geral de Depositos, Novo Banco, ActivoBank cited by guides.
restrictions: NIF required first; strict AML and CRS reporting; US persons face FATCA scrutiny.
alternatives: Remote-opening intermediaries; Wise, Revolut (EUR IBAN).
cost_note: Opening deposit of about EUR 250 at some banks such as Millennium bcp/CGD (EUR 1 = USD 1.17); the bank opening fee is not published, intermediary remote-opening packages cost about EUR 270-700 (USD 315-820), and monthly fees vary by bank (web search budget exhausted in pass 2, so figures come from the existing min_deposit_fees text and were not re-verified against a bank tariff).

documents: Kuwaiti civil ID, residence visa, employer No Objection Certificate, passport, salary certificate.
banks: none known for non-resident personal accounts; NBK, Gulf Bank, KFH require civil ID.
restrictions: Personal accounts tied to residency and civil ID; digital onboarding needs civil ID face match; brokerage accounts (e.g. KMEFIC) may accept embassy-attested passports.
alternatives: Kuwaiti brokerage accounts; KFH UK subsidiary; Wise/Revolut held abroad.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts here (NBK, Gulf Bank and KFH require a Kuwaiti civil ID), so no costs apply.

documents: Passport and Libyan residence papers; local address and in-branch visit.
banks: none known for non-residents; Aman Bank, Jumhouria Bank, National Commercial Bank serve residents.
restrictions: Political division and conflict; Central Bank of Libya FX controls, cash shortages and dual exchange rates; foreigners reported refused locally; heavy de-risking by correspondents.
alternatives: Offshore/international accounts; Western Union and MoneyGram transfers with limits.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts here (local banks serve residents only), so no costs apply.

documents: Passport or national ID, proof of address; Central Bank of Somalia requires national ID for new accounts in Banadir region.
banks: none known for non-Somali foreigners; Dahabshil Bank, Premier Bank, Salaam Somali Bank, IBS target Somalis and diaspora.
restrictions: High-risk jurisdiction with limited correspondent banking; Al-Shabaab-related sanctions/AML scrutiny; economy largely USD and mobile money.
alternatives: Mobile money (EVC Plus, Zaad) and hawala remittance (Dahabshiil) via local SIM/contacts.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts here (banks serve Somalis and the diaspora, not other foreigners), so no costs apply.

documents: Passport with valid Nepal visa, photos, application form, proof of address; account validity tied to visa period.
banks: Commercial banks licensed by Nepal Rastra Bank case-by-case; Machhapuchchhre Bank offers NRN foreign-currency accounts for those of Nepali origin.
restrictions: NRB rules: tourist accounts valid only until visa expiry; NPR not freely convertible; foreign-currency withdrawal limits.
alternatives: Wise and remittance services; eSewa/Khalti wallets need local ID.
cost_note: Commercial banks open case-by-case and publish no non-resident opening fee, minimum deposit or monthly fee, and NRN accounts are for people of Nepali origin (web search budget exhausted in pass 2, so figures come from the existing min_deposit_fees text and were not re-verified against a bank tariff).

documents: Passport, proof of address, and justification of purpose under BCEAO non-resident account rules; details not published by banks.
banks: none known specifically; Coris Bank International and Ecobank Burkina operate but publish no non-resident terms.
restrictions: BCEAO Instruction 09/07/2025/RFE governs non-resident foreign accounts and FX accounts; military government and security situation; heightened AML scrutiny.
alternatives: Mobile money (Orange Money, Moov Money) with local SIM; Wise/remittance services.
cost_note: Coris Bank International and Ecobank Burkina publish no non-resident opening fee, minimum deposit or monthly fee (web search budget exhausted in pass 2, so figures come from the existing min_deposit_fees text and were not re-verified against a bank tariff).

documents: Not applicable; historically only resident diplomats and aid workers could open foreign-currency accounts (e.g. Narae card).
banks: none known; Foreign Trade Bank and others are UN/US/Australian sanctioned.
restrictions: Comprehensive UN, US and Australian autonomous sanctions; dealings with DPRK banks prohibited for Australians; no correspondent banking.
alternatives: none
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts here (all banks are under UN/US/Australian sanctions), so no costs apply.
